# Sutanujātaka (Ja 398)

**ID:** Ja 398
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Sutanujātaka
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul6.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sutanujātaka* (Ja 398) is a canonical birth tale in the Pali Jātaka collection. According to its nidāna framework, the Buddha recounted this story while dwelling at Jetavana regarding a monk who dutifully supported his mother, an introductory circumstance noted as recurring in the Sāma Birth (*Sāmajātaka*). In the story's index entry, the titular protagonist Sutanu (or Sutano), a young man (*māṇava*) born into a poor householder's family (*duggata-gahapatiputta*), is identified as the Bodhisatta [Fausböll 1897]. Later Ceylonese historical tradition records the prominence of the text: according to the *Cūḷavaṁsa*, the *Sutanujātaka* was one of thirty-two selected birth tales depicted in coloured paintings on the walls of a courtyard [Geiger 1953].

**Sources**

- [Fausböll 1897] V. Fausböll, Jātaka Together with Its Commentary, Vol. 7 (Index) (1897) — Identification of Sutanu as the Bodhisatta and son of a poor householder.
- [Geiger 1953] Wilhelm Geiger (tr.), Cūḷavaṁsa, Part 1 (1953) — Record of the Sutanujātaka being depicted among thirty-two jātaka courtyard wall paintings.
